title: InjectionSource enum in core and NntpQueue envelope field
description:
Define the InjectionSource type and thread it through the NntpQueue envelope.

What: crates/core/src/injection_source.rs; crates/smtp/src/relay_queue.rs (NntpQueue envelope)

InjectionSource (core):
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub enum InjectionSource {
      NntpPost,        // direct NNTP POST command
      SmtpNewsgroups,  // SMTP message with explicit Newsgroups: header
      SmtpSieve,       // SMTP routed by sieve fileinto "newsgroup:..."
      SmtpListId,      // SMTP routed by List-ID fallback (local-only)
  }
  impl InjectionSource {
      pub fn is_peerable(&self) -> bool {
          !matches!(self, Self::SmtpListId)
      }
  }
  pub use in crates/core/src/lib.rs

NntpQueue envelope (crates/smtp — the JSON .env file written alongside .msg):
  Add field: injection_source: InjectionSource  (default SmtpSieve for backward compat with existing queue files that lack the field)
  The sieve session sets this when enqueuing:
    - FileInto("newsgroup:...") from sieve script    → SmtpSieve
    - FileInto("newsgroup:...") from List-ID fallback → SmtpListId
    - FileInto("newsgroup:...") from Newsgroups: header fallback → SmtpNewsgroups

Algorithm:
1. Add InjectionSource to core/src/lib.rs.
2. Add injection_source: InjectionSource field to the NntpQueue envelope struct in smtp.
3. Add #[serde(default = "default_injection_source")] with default = SmtpSieve so old queue files deserialize cleanly.
4. Update all enqueue call sites in smtp/src/session.rs to pass the correct source.

Defensive rules:
- serde default ensures backward compat with queue files written before this change.
- is_peerable() is the single authoritative check; no other code should pattern-match on the enum for routing decisions.
